cards.title: Three ways to talk about the future
cards.body: Present + future context, ir a + verb (used even more than in English), or the future tense. Bailar = to dance (bailarín = dancer, hence 'ballerina').

examples.es: Bailamos más tarde. / Vamos a bailar más tarde.

cards.title: Future: bailaré
cards.body: Add the haber sounds to the whole verb and stress the ending.

examples.en: I / we / he / they / you will dance

cards.title: 'Would' = whole verb + -ía
cards.body: -ía covers I and he/she/it/formal you. Then -íamos, -ían, -ías, with the stress always on the í. One set of endings for all verb types, as with 'will'.

examples.en: I'd eat, but I don't have time.

cards.title: 'Gets transformed' = transforms itself
cards.body: Spanish has no 'get' for 'gets done'. It uses se ('itself'), which doesn't mean the thing does it to itself.

cards.title: se contamina = it gets contaminated
cards.body: The river 'contaminates itself' simply means it gets contaminated.

cards.title: me imagino
cards.body: Sometimes adding -self barely changes the meaning: imagino = me imagino.

examples.en: I'd imagine he doesn't want to go.
examples.es: Me imaginaría que no quiere ir.

practice.en: I'd eat, but I don't have time.
I'd imagine he doesn't want to go.
es: Me imaginaría que no quiere ir
practice.why: me imaginaría + que + no quiere ir.
